- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk aversion or market correction.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the 10–15 day horizon after spikes; add 2–5% buffer to forecast for mean reversion or momentum carry.
- In 30-day forecasts, model frequently misses late-period upward momentum; increase final 5–7 days of forecast slope if sentiment turns bullish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to be overly conservative; introduce mild upward bias (e.g., +1–2%) to avoid prolonged flatness.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive over 3–5 days, model lags in adjusting; apply early correction to forecast 2–3 days ahead of true trend.
